rationale: Evaluating whether required braking maneuvers are omitted requires characterising the vehicle’s braking response in situations requiring collision avoidance. SG-1 and FR-7 establish that response itself as part of the evaluation, while H-1 supports the road-user/static-obstacle scope and the pedestrian scenario. P does not expand the phenomenon to sensing, computation, communication, failure mitigation, or mechanism-level timing merely because these can influence braking.
determining_elements: “The vehicle’s braking-relevant response” identifies behaviour directly required by SG-1 and FR-7, rather than adding unrelated system-response behaviour.
“Where braking may be required to avoid collision” ties the response to the condition relevant to evaluating omitted required braking.
The scope covers road users and static obstacles, including the pedestrian crossing 20 m ahead on a straight single-lane road; these are supported by H-1.
The scope describes situations requiring evaluation of braking necessity without incorporating the internal mechanisms performing that evaluation.
